endorsements.quote: For example, personnel responsible for assessment of proposed AI tools can use a standardized protocol to evaluate the sponsorship, quality, performance, and planned use of every AI tool, whether it is a relatively minor feature built into a radiological device or a predictive risk scoring tool that will impact patient triage and care.
We propose that similar impact statements should be created before AI-based tool deployment decisions are finalized.
These Model Facts Labels should be structured to allow continuous learning for each of the target audiences, and ideally would be required for regulatory approval.

Because of this drift, organizations will need routines not only for the initial evaluation and implementation of new AI-based algorithms and tools, but also for maintaining them and monitoring their outputs.
All these activities will require dedicated resources to implement effectively.

unlisted_practices: Establish integrated organizational routines for the assessment, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of AI-based resources.
Develop standards for AI reporting and evaluation, such as Model Facts Labels and Health Ecosystem Impact Statements.
Establish a transparent FDA process for review and approval of algorithms.
Develop ethical and legal frameworks for patient rights and use of data.
Continually invest in and iteratively improve national regulatory infrastructures to keep pace with AI development.
Build shared debiasing infrastructures to support evidence-based practice, systemic evaluation, and continuous improvement.
Foster interorganizational collaboration among technical and health professionals, patients, administrators, and peer institutions to design, evaluate, and improve AI.
Share AI management expertise across health systems or regions to help under-resourced organizations become AI-capable.
Health-related professional organizations should establish ownership of AI management issues to provide thought leadership and policy guidance.
Create AI curricular elements in healthcare management training programs.
Develop systematic learning programs and competencies to prepare clinicians to evaluate and safely use AI-based tools.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper providing guidance and recommendations on organizational capabilities, governance, and infrastructure needed for safe AI deployment in health care.
